decisions.statement: The subagent stopped is named by the first word.
A subagent to stop is named as that subagent's page is named.
A name no subagent has a page for is refused as data.
A stop is written beside the subagent's page rather than into that page.
A subagent stopped already is left as it is, and the run says so.
The report says when the stop reaches the subagent.
A stop reaches the subagent at its next model turn.
A subagent inside a tool call finishes that call before the stop reaches it.
A run censuses the subagent's page before writing the stop.
The census is taken before the stop, so the stop never decides that census.
A page the census judges stale is taken away by this run.
A page the census judges working or undetermined is left where it is.
The stop is written before any page is taken away.
A page the index files no subagent for is judged nothing and left where it is.
A census that will not read leaves the judgement the processes alone reached.
A page left here goes as the gateway refuses the turn that stop ends it on.
A page neither route takes goes at the next sweep, on the stop written here.

definition: the command stopping a subagent by refusing the model turns that subagent asks for
